title: Actual image subsheaves give small sectionwise representatives for subobjects on a small ringed site
statement: Fix a Grothendieck universe $\mathcal V$ [def-weil-size-convention], a $\mathcal V$-small site $\mathcal C$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] with object set $K\in\mathcal V$, and a sheaf of rings $R$ whose section sets lie in $\mathcal V$. All module sheaves have section sets in $\mathcal V$ and mean sectionwise modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $J\in\mathcal V$ and $(P_j)_{j\in J}$ be any family of $R$-module sheaves. Put $D_j=\prod_{V\in K}\mathcal P(P_j(V))$ and let $E_j\subseteq D_j$ consist of families $(N_V)_V$ such that each $N_V$ is an $R(V)$-submodule of $P_j(V)$, restrictions of $P_j$ preserve these subsets, and the resulting presheaf $N$ satisfies the sheaf axiom. Each such code determines a unique module subsheaf $N\subseteq P_j$ with the inherited operations, and its inclusion is a monomorphism. For every monomorphism $m:M\to P_j$, the sectionwise maps $m_V$ are injective, the family $N_V=m_V(M(V))$ belongs to $E_j$, and the induced sectionwise bijections give a module-sheaf isomorphism $e:M\xrightarrow{\sim}N$ with $\iota_N\circ e=m$. Two monomorphisms into $P_j$ are isomorphic over $P_j$ if and only if their sectionwise image families are equal. Conversely every code in $E_j$ is the image family of its own inclusion. The sets $D_j$, $E_j$ and $\coprod_{j\in J}E_j$ belong to $\mathcal V$. Thus the latter set indexes actual image subsheaves representing every subobject of every $P_j$, up to isomorphism over its specified target. This is an assertion about sectionwise images of monomorphisms, and makes no claim that the sectionwise image of an arbitrary sheaf morphism is a sheaf.

proof.text: Fix $j$. For a code $(N_V)_V\in E_j$, give $N(V)=N_V$ the addition and $R(V)$-action restricted from $P_j(V)$ and restrict $P_j(f)$ to these subsets for every arrow $f:W\to V$. Stability under restrictions makes these maps well-defined; identity, composition and semilinearity hold because they hold in $P_j$. The sheaf axiom is part of membership in $E_j$. Thus [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] gives an actual module sheaf with inclusion $\iota_N$. These inherited operations and maps leave no choice in the subsheaf determined by the code. If $a,b:T\to N$ satisfy $\iota_Na=\iota_Nb$, then $a_V(t)=b_V(t)$ in the subset $N_V$ for every $V,t$, so $a=b$. Hence $\iota_N$ is monic.

source.place: Paragraph (2), final sentence, expanded: interpreting sectionwise subset codes with inherited module operations.

proof.text: For a monomorphism m of module sheaves, the forgetful functor to presheaves of modules preserves finite limits, hence preserves monomorphisms. Apply Mathlib PresheafOfModules.injective_of_mono to its underlying morphism to obtain injectivity on every section module. This implements the sectionwise-kernel argument of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], Stacks Tag 03DA, using the existing Mathlib limits API.

proof.text: Set $N_V=\{m_V(x):x\in M(V)\}$. The identities $m_V(0)=0$, $m_V(x+y)=m_V(x)+m_V(y)$, $m_V(-x)=-m_V(x)$ and $m_V(ax)=a m_V(x)$ show that $N_V$ is an $R(V)$-submodule. For $f:W\to V$, naturality gives $P_j(f)(m_V(x))=m_W(M(f)(x))\in N_W$. Thus these ranges form a presheaf with inherited module structure as in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Paragraph (2), final sentence, expanded: ranges and inherited restriction maps.

proof.text: Before imposing the sheaf condition on the range presheaf N of step 3, construct a presheaf isomorphism e from M to N. At X use LinearEquiv.ofInjective on m_X, bundled with LinearEquiv.toModuleIso; naturality follows pointwise from naturality of m and injectivity of the subtype inclusion. PresheafOfModules.isoMk supplies the natural inverse. Map this isomorphism to presheaves of abelian groups and use Presheaf.isSheaf_of_iso_iff to transfer the sheaf condition of M to N. This is the matching-family transport of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], including empty coverings, packaged by the existing sheaf invariance lemma.

source.place: Paragraph (2), final sentence, expanded: transport of the sheaf axiom to actual ranges of monomorphisms.

proof.text: Package the sectionwise ranges as a ModuleSubsheafCode using the explicit submodule N and its proved sheaf condition. Submodule.ext and SetLike.coe_injective show that the submodule recovered from that code equals N, because their carriers agree. Transport the presheaf isomorphism of step 4 along this equality and lift it to module sheaves by fullyFaithfulForget.preimageIso. Its composite with the subset inclusion equals m pointwise. Evaluating this equality proves the stated formula on every section. These constructions use [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with no arbitrary choice of an image object.

source.place: Paragraph (2), final sentence, expanded: natural linear inverse and factorization over the specified target.

proof.text: If monomorphisms $m:M\to P_j$ and $m':M'\to P_j$ are isomorphic over $P_j$ by $h:M\xrightarrow{\sim}M'$ with $m'h=m$, then $h_V$ is surjective (its inverse is the component of $h^{-1}$), so their sectionwise ranges are equal. Conversely, if their image families agree, the isomorphisms $e,e'$ of step 5 have the same actual subsheaf as codomain, and $(e')^{-1}e$ is an isomorphism over $P_j$. For any code, the range of its inclusion on $V$ is exactly $N_V$. Together with step 1 this proves both the equivalence criterion and realization of every code.

source.place: Paragraph (2), final sentence, expanded: uniqueness up to isomorphism over a fixed target and realization of every code.

proof.text: Use the Grothendieck-universe convention [def-weil-size-convention] and the size hypotheses of the item. Powerset closure gives $\mathcal P(P_j(V))\in\mathcal V$. Closure under unions indexed by the set $K\in\mathcal V$ gives $T_j=\bigcup_{V\in K}\mathcal P(P_j(V))\in\mathcal V$. Every family in $D_j$ is its graph in $K\times T_j$, so $D_j\subseteq\mathcal P(K\times T_j)$ and $D_j\in\mathcal V$ by powerset closure and transitivity. As $E_j\subseteq D_j$, the same axioms give $E_j\in\mathcal V$. Finally closure under $J$-indexed unions and ordered pairs gives $\coprod_{j\in J}E_j=\{(j,N):j\in J,\ N\in E_j\}\in\mathcal V$. By steps 1 and 5 this set indexes actual subsheaves representing all subobjects with their specified target. For $J=\varnothing$ it is empty; for $K=\varnothing$ each $D_j$ and $E_j$ consists of the empty family; for a zero target there is just the zero subsheaf. No step used a sectionwise-image assertion for a nonmonic map.
